title: Exemestane · daily hormone therapy
context_label: Postmenopausal ER-positive breast cancer after prior endocrine treatment
schedule_summary: Take exemestane once daily continuously, preferably after a meal. There is no planned week off. Confirm the prior-treatment and duration plan.
purpose: After early breast cancer treatment, endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence. In advanced disease, the aim is to control cancer and symptoms. Your setting determines the duration and follow-up.
indication_text: Exemestane is used for selected postmenopausal hormone-sensitive breast cancer after surgery, as extended endocrine treatment or for advanced disease after earlier treatment. The team checks which previous endocrine medicine you received and why a switch or extension is appropriate. If switching after tamoxifen, the earlier years count towards the intended total treatment plan.
administration_text: Swallow the tablet whole, preferably after a meal; do not chew or crush it. Skip a missed dose and continue at the next scheduled time; do not double the dose.
monitoring_summary: FBC, renal and liver profile, confirmation of menopause when uncertain, and bone / fracture assessment. Consider baseline vitamin D as specified by the product information. The NICE adjuvant baseline-DXA recommendation has an exception for patients already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates. Review symptoms, adherence and bone health. Repeat bone density and lipids when indicated; assess other blood tests according to the clinical plan.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.mechanism: Reduces the oestrogen available to stimulate cancer cells
agents.explanation: Exemestane switches off aromatase, the enzyme that makes oestrogen in tissues after menopause. This reduces the hormone signal that can encourage hormone-sensitive breast cancer cells to grow. The body makes new enzyme over time, so tablets must still follow the prescribed daily schedule. It does not reliably switch off functioning ovaries; any ovarian suppression must be prescribed and checked separately.
agents.watch: Tell the team if joint pain, hot flushes, vaginal dryness or sleep disturbance affects daily life. Bone thinning may cause no early symptoms, so keep the agreed bone-health reviews.
risks: Joint and muscle pain or stiffness
Hot flushes, sleep disturbance and fatigue
Uncommon liver abnormalities or serious allergic reactions

sections.title: Take after food
sections.text: A regular meal can anchor the daily dose. Do not compensate for a missed tablet with a double dose.

sections.title: Count the whole endocrine course
sections.text: In an adjuvant switch, the earlier tamoxifen years count towards the intended total. Switching medicines does not automatically restart a five-year clock.

sections.title: Bone and vitamin D
sections.text: Ask about baseline DXA, vitamin D assessment if appropriate, and the result-review plan. Supplements or antiresorptive drugs should follow the individual plan.

sections.title: Medicine interactions
sections.text: Strong enzyme-inducing medicines can reduce exposure. Ask the pharmacy to check all medicines and supplements before starting or changing them.

evidence.title: Why this endocrine treatment is offered
evidence.population: Evidence depends on the treatment setting and previous endocrine medicines.
evidence.interpretation: For hormone-sensitive early breast cancer, endocrine treatment helps reduce the chance of the cancer returning. For advanced disease, it can help control cancer and symptoms.
evidence.limitations: Your likely benefit depends on your cancer, previous treatment and health. The treating team explains why this option fits your plan.

teachback: What is your treatment schedule, which checks apply to your setting, and who books and reviews them?
consent_support: The kidney and liver advice for exemestane differs from some other aromatase inhibitors: a routine dose reduction is not specified, but organ problems still need clinical review. Tell the pharmacist about all medicines and supplements because some can make exemestane less effective. Do not increase the dose yourself. Confirm menopause and any separate ovarian-suppression plan.

support.title: Symptoms and daily life
support.text: Tell the team if joint pain, hot flushes, vaginal dryness or sleep disturbance affects daily life. Bone thinning may cause no early symptoms, so keep the agreed bone-health reviews.

support.title: Support medicines
support.text: No routine antiemetic, steroid premedication or G-CSF is required by this endocrine monotherapy. Ask for individual symptom support.

support.title: Tests and appointments
support.text: Ask who books each check, when it is due and who reviews it. Tell the team if an expected appointment has not arrived.

items.title: Who this information covers
items.text: Exemestane is used for selected postmenopausal hormone-sensitive breast cancer after surgery, as extended endocrine treatment or for advanced disease after earlier treatment. The team checks which previous endocrine medicine you received and why a switch or extension is appropriate. If switching after tamoxifen, the earlier years count towards the intended total treatment plan.

items.title: Medicine and schedule
items.text: Take exemestane once daily continuously, preferably after a meal. There is no planned week off. Confirm the prior-treatment and duration plan. Swallow the tablet whole, preferably after a meal; do not chew or crush it. Skip a missed dose and continue at the next scheduled time; do not double the dose.

items.title: Review and duration
items.text: Swallow the tablet whole, preferably after a meal; do not chew or crush it. Skip a missed dose and continue at the next scheduled time; do not double the dose. Count earlier endocrine treatment when reviewing an adjuvant switch. Extended treatment is a separate decision.

items.title: Individual risks and support
items.text: The kidney and liver advice for exemestane differs from some other aromatase inhibitors: a routine dose reduction is not specified, but organ problems still need clinical review. Tell the pharmacist about all medicines and supplements because some can make exemestane less effective. Do not increase the dose yourself. Confirm menopause and any separate ovarian-suppression plan.

chapters.title: Checks throughout treatment
chapters.intro: Your team arranges tests and explains the results. A planned check is not confirmation that it has been completed.

items.title: Treatment-specific checks
items.text: FBC, renal and liver profile, confirmation of menopause when uncertain, and bone / fracture assessment. Consider baseline vitamin D as specified by the product information. The NICE adjuvant baseline-DXA recommendation has an exception for patients already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates. Review symptoms, adherence and bone health. Repeat bone density and lipids when indicated; assess other blood tests according to the clinical plan.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: ECG or other heart tests depend on symptoms and personal risk; this medicine alone does not require a routine HER2-style echocardiogram schedule.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Offer baseline DXA when starting an adjuvant aromatase inhibitor if not already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates; assess fracture risk and relevant previous results. Under the 2025 joint guidance, patients with a T-score above −2.0 and no additional risk factors generally have risk and bone density reassessed every one to two years. Patients on bone-protective treatment generally have BMD reassessed about every two years. Fracture, substantial bone loss or a change in risk can require earlier review. The clinician selects the interval and any bone treatment; these are not automatic yearly scans for everyone.

chapters.title: Your setting changes the pathway
chapters.intro: Choose the pathway that your team has confirmed; these are not all extra treatments you must have.

items.title: Early-breast follow-up
items.text: After curative treatment, annual mammography is generally used for remaining breast tissue: both breasts after conservation or the opposite breast after unilateral mastectomy. The mastectomy side is not routinely mammographed. Routine CT, bone scans and tumour markers are not recommended for asymptomatic early-breast surveillance. New symptoms need assessment between appointments.

items.title: Surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy
items.text: In an early-breast pathway, chemotherapy, if indicated, precedes endocrine treatment. Surgery and its pathology guide adjuvant choices. Postoperative radiotherapy is usually delivered after recovery and any adjuvant chemotherapy; aromatase inhibitors may overlap radiotherapy under the agreed plan. Tamoxifen timing around radiotherapy is agreed by the treating teams. None of these additional treatments is automatically required by an endocrine prescription.

items.title: Advanced-disease scans
items.text: For advanced breast cancer, response assessment is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease pace, sites, symptoms and treatment. Indolent disease may be reviewed less often; new symptoms can prompt earlier scans. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not a universal three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: Tumour markers may supplement imaging and clinical assessment in advanced disease if they are informative, especially if elevated at baseline. They do not replace scans, and a marker change alone should not determine treatment failure. There is no universal fixed marker timetable.

items.title: Menopause, pregnancy and contraception
items.text: Confirm the postmenopausal endocrine state. Any ovarian-suppression combination needs a separate prescription and monitoring plan.

questions.a: Take exemestane once daily continuously, preferably after a meal. There is no planned week off. Confirm the prior-treatment and duration plan.

questions.q: When are bloods, ECGs or echoes needed?
questions.a: FBC, renal and liver profile, confirmation of menopause when uncertain, and bone / fracture assessment. Consider baseline vitamin D as specified by the product information. The NICE adjuvant baseline-DXA recommendation has an exception for patients already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates. Review symptoms, adherence and bone health. Repeat bone density and lipids when indicated; assess other blood tests according to the clinical plan. There is no routine ECG or echo schedule for exemestane alone. Investigate symptoms and manage cardiovascular risk when indicated.

The mastectomy side is not routinely mammographed. Routine CT, bone scans and tumour markers are not recommended for asymptomatic early-breast surveillance. New symptoms need assessment between appointments. For advanced breast cancer, response assessment is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease pace, sites, symptoms and treatment. Offer baseline DXA when starting an adjuvant aromatase inhibitor if not already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates; assess fracture risk and relevant previous results. The clinician selects the interval and any bone treatment; these are not automatic yearly scans for everyone.

If you switch after tamoxifen, the earlier years count towards the intended total endocrine course. Switching does not automatically mean starting a new full course. The team confirms your intended total and whether a later extension is appropriate. Advanced-disease treatment continues according to benefit and tolerance.

questions.q: Do I need a port or home pump?
questions.a: No port or home infusion pump is needed for this medicine itself. Any separately prescribed medicine has its own access requirements.

questions.q: Can I use HRT, vaginal oestrogen or supplements?
questions.a: Check with the oncology team before starting any hormone-containing treatment, including vaginal oestrogen, or any new medicine or supplement. Some can oppose this treatment or change how it works. The team can suggest symptom treatments and decide whether specialist review is needed.

questions.q: What if periods return or menopause is uncertain?
questions.a: Tell the team promptly about a return of periods or new vaginal bleeding. No periods after chemotherapy does not always mean the ovaries have permanently stopped working. Hormone blood tests may be needed. Ovarian suppression, if prescribed, has its own schedule and monitoring.

questions.q: What should I do if symptoms make tablets difficult to continue?
questions.a: Tell the team early about joint pain, hot flushes, sleep, vaginal or sexual symptoms, fatigue or missed tablets. Support, a supervised break or a change of medicine may be possible. Agree the plan with the prescriber rather than changing or stopping treatment yourself.

questions.q: Can another medicine make exemestane less effective?
questions.a: Yes. Some medicines for seizures or infections, and St John’s wort, can reduce its effect. Check every new prescription, over-the-counter medicine and supplement with the oncology pharmacist. Do not compensate by taking extra exemestane.

questions.q: Do I need calcium and vitamin D?
questions.a: The NCCP regimen advises daily calcium and vitamin D supplementation. Ask the team or pharmacist to confirm the suitable product and dose, taking account of your diet, blood results, kidney health and any supplements you already take. Bone-protective medicines and bone-density checks follow your individual fracture-risk plan.
